question:
This passage comes from Lilliam Rivera's 2020 novel Never Look Back, in which the narrator describes arriving at his father's apartment.

"Pops, I'm here!" I drop my bag and set my guitar case against a wall. I place my keys on the bowl right next to the ceramic elephant Pops got me on one of his trips to Santo Domingo when I was a little kid.

©2020 by Lilliam Rivera

As used in the text, what does the word "place" most nearly mean?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The narrator sets his keys down on the bowl, so "place" means to put or set something down.
longexplanation: In context, the narrator lists a sequence of homecoming actions—dropping his bag, setting his guitar case against a wall, and then setting his keys onto the bowl. "Place" here describes putting the keys in a particular spot, which matches "Put." The alternatives "Remove," "Rank," and "Unfold" do not fit the action of setting keys onto a bowl. Substituting "put" for "place" keeps the sentence's meaning intact.

question:
This passage is from Kenneth Grahame's 1908 novel The Wind in the Willows. The Mole is on his way home following a visit to Mr. Badger's house.

As he hurried along, eagerly anticipating the moment when he would be at home again among the things he knew and liked, the Mole saw clearly that he was an animal of tilled field and hedge-row, linked to the ploughed furrow, the frequented pasture, the lane of evening lingerings, the cultivated garden-plot.

As used in the text, what does the word "anticipating" most nearly mean?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The Mole is eagerly awaiting the moment he will be home, so "anticipating" means looking forward to.
longexplanation: The word "eagerly" signals that the Mole feels excitement about a future event—being home again among familiar things. "Anticipating" therefore conveys pleasurable expectation, matching "Looking forward to." "Describing" and "Instructing" involve communication rather than expectation, and "Getting ahead of" implies moving past something, neither of which fits the Mole's hopeful mood. Only "Looking forward to" preserves the sense of eager expectation.

question:
First proposed in 1970, McMullen's g-conjecture _______ many mathematicians for decades until it finally yielded to the work of Karim Adiprasito, who published a proof in 2018.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The conjecture resisted proof for decades before finally being solved, so it "confounded" mathematicians.
longexplanation: The sentence contrasts a long period of difficulty with the eventual proof in 2018 ("until it finally yielded"), so the missing word should mean the conjecture puzzled or baffled mathematicians. "Confounded" captures that sense of frustrating and defeating attempts to solve it. "Appeased" (satisfied) and "disregarded" (ignored) contradict the effort implied by the sentence, and "indoctrinated" (taught a set of beliefs) makes no sense with a conjecture as the subject. Only "confounded" fits the logic of a hard problem that resisted solution.

question:
The Nobel Prize in Chemistry is often awarded to a single person, as it was to Frederick Sanger in 1958. At other times, however, the Nobel Committee wishes to honor work credited to two or three individuals, in which case the prize is awarded _____. In 2008, for example, Roger Y. Tsien was among the recipients recognized for "the discovery and development of the green fluorescent protein, GFP."

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: When the prize honors work by two or three people, it is shared among them, so it is awarded "jointly."
longexplanation: The sentence describes cases in which the prize recognizes work by more than one person, illustrated by Tsien being "among the recipients" in 2008. The blank needs a word meaning that the award is shared, which is exactly what "jointly" means. "Ceremoniously" describes manner, "reluctantly" adds an unsupported negative attitude, and "retroactively" refers to timing—none of these captures the idea of sharing an award. Only "jointly" matches the context of a prize divided among several people.

question:
This passage is from Yung Wing's 1909 memoir My Life in China and America. Yung Wing was the first person of Chinese heritage to graduate from an American college; Phoebe Brown was the first prominent female hymn writer in the United States.

I look back upon my acquaintance with Mrs. Phoebe H. Brown with a mingled feeling of respect and admiration. She certainly was a remarkable New England woman—a woman of surpassing strength of moral and religious character. Those who have had the rare privilege of reading her stirring biography, will, I am sure, bear me out in this statement. She went through the crucible of unprecedented adversities and trials of life and came out one of the rare shining lights that beautify the New England sky.

Which choice best describes the function of the reference to Brown's biography in the passage as a whole?
option a: It emphasizes that Brown's life has been a popular subject for writers because it was so remarkable.
option b: It suggests that other people who are familiar with Brown's life would share the author's view of her.
option c: It explains why Brown was unique amongst her peers.
option d: It describes the nature of the relationship between Yung and Brown.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Yung says readers of Brown's biography would "bear me out," implying they would agree with his admiring view.
longexplanation: The reference to the biography appears in the clause "Those who have had the rare privilege of reading her stirring biography, will... bear me out in this statement." Yung uses this to claim that anyone who knows Brown's life would confirm his high opinion of her strength and character. This directly supports choice B. The passage never says the biography made Brown a popular literary subject (A) or that it explains her uniqueness among peers (C), and it points to readers' agreement rather than the Yung–Brown relationship itself (D).

question:
A loanword is a word that originates in one language and is later adopted by another; "cocoa" is one example. English acquired the word indirectly from cacao, the Spanish name for the plant that chocolate is made from. Spanish, in turn, had borrowed it from Nahuatl, an Indigenous language of Central Mexico, in which the word originally appears as cacahuatl. "Maize" likewise has Indigenous roots and entered English by way of Spanish, but here the ultimate source was Taino, a language of the Caribbean islands, in which the word for the corn plant is mahis.

The author makes which point about the Spanish language?
option a: It adopted Nahuatl and Taino words in approximately equal numbers.
option b: It has served as a medium through which Indigenous languages have influenced English.
option c: Its contribution to English vocabulary roughly equals the collective contribution by Indigenous languages.
option d: It has borrowed words from Indigenous languages and contributed words to them.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: In both examples, Indigenous words reached English by passing through Spanish, making Spanish the channel of influence.
longexplanation: The passage traces two words—"cocoa" from Nahuatl and "maize" from Taino—each of which entered English only after Spanish borrowed it first. This pattern shows Spanish acting as an intermediary that carried Indigenous words into English, which is what choice B states. The text gives no counts to support the "equal numbers" claim (A) and no comparison of overall vocabulary contributions (C). It also never says Spanish gave words back to Indigenous languages (D), so only B is supported.

question:
"A Pair of Silk Stockings" is an 1897 short story by Kate Chopin. In the story, Mrs. Sommers attends a play that she experiences as a brief escape from the circumstances of her everyday life: ______

Which quotation from "A Pair of Silk Stockings" most effectively illustrates the claim?
option a: "The play was over, the music ceased, the crowd filed out. It was like a dream ended."
option b: "But there were vacant seats here and there, and into one of them she was ushered, between brilliantly dressed women who had gone there to kill time and eat candy and display their gaudy attire."
option c: "It was a little later when she entered the theatre, the play had begun and the house seemed to her to be packed."
option d: "When she entered [the restaurant] her appearance created no surprise, no consternation, as she had half feared it might."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Comparing the play's end to a dream ending shows Mrs. Sommers treated it as a temporary escape from reality.
longexplanation: The claim is that the play offers Mrs. Sommers a brief escape from her ordinary life. Choice A directly supports this by likening the moment the play ends to "a dream ended," framing the experience as a dreamlike break that must now conclude. The other quotations describe seating and the crowd (B), her arrival timing (C), or her entrance into a restaurant (D), none of which conveys escape or its ending. Only A ties the theatrical experience to a temporary, dreamlike reprieve.

question:
Eastern North Pacific (ENP) gray whales generally migrate between their wintering waters along the coast of Mexico and their foraging waters in the Arctic. However, a portion of this population—the Pacific Coast Feeding Group (PCFG)—instead forages along the coastlines of Northern California (USA) and British Columbia (Canada). Notably, whales in this subset reach smaller maximum sizes than other ENP whales do, even though their growth rates before reaching that maximum are similar. Researchers hypothesize that this size difference may be an adaptation to the distinct feeding opportunities available in the PCFG's range.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' claim regarding the size of PCFG whales?
option a: When foraging along the coasts of Northern California and British Columbia, PCFG whales are in closer proximity to major ports and urban populations than ENP whales in the main group are when foraging in Arctic waters.
option b: The average body size of PCFG whales observed along the coasts of Northern California and British Columbia has remained relatively steady in recent decades, while the average body size of ENP whales in the main group has slightly decreased.
option c: When present along the coasts of Northern California and British Columbia, PCFG whales tend to forage in rocky kelp beds at shallow depths inaccessible to whales as large as those in the ENP main group.
option d: Certain crustacean prey species available along the coasts of Northern California and British Columbia where PCFG whales tend to forage are not available in the Arctic waters where ENP whales in the main group forage.
subject: Reading and Writing
tags: command of evidence, quantitative and scientific reasoning
shortexplanation: If smaller size lets PCFG whales reach food in shallow kelp beds that larger whales cannot, then their size is an adaptation to their feeding range.
longexplanation: The researchers claim that the smaller size of PCFG whales is an adaptation to distinct resource opportunities in their foraging range. Choice C supports this by showing that a smaller body allows PCFG whales to feed in shallow, rocky kelp beds that larger ENP whales cannot reach—directly linking reduced size to a feeding advantage. Choices A and B describe proximity to ports and body-size trends over time, neither of which connects size to feeding opportunities. Choice D shows different prey exist but does not explain why smaller size would be advantageous, so only C provides the needed support.

question:
Benjamin S. Turner, an Alabama resident sworn in as a member of the US House of Representatives in 1871, was one of the nearly two thousand African ______ in the decade following the Civil War.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No possession or contraction is needed, so both plural nouns take a simple -s with no apostrophe.
longexplanation: The sentence refers to "nearly two thousand African Americans" (a plural group) "who won elections" (plural events), and neither noun shows possession or forms a contraction. Therefore no apostrophes are required, which makes choice D correct. Choices A and C add possessive apostrophes to "Americans"/"American" that have nothing to possess, and choices A and B insert apostrophes into "elections"/"election" where a plain plural is needed. Only D uses standard plural forms without stray apostrophes.

question:
Having devised an optical spectroscopy technique that allowed researchers to study the ultrafast chemical reactions occurring within molecules, ______ known as femtochemistry. For this pioneering work, he received the Othmer Gold Medal and the Davy Medal from the Royal Society.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
option a: chemist Ahmed Zewail introduced a new scientific discipline
option b: a new scientific discipline was introduced by Ahmed Zewail, a chemist
option c: the introduction of a new scientific discipline was initiated by chemist Ahmed Zewail
option d: chemist Ahmed Zewail's introduction of a new scientific discipline would be
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The introductory modifier must describe the person who devised the technique, so "chemist Ahmed Zewail" must follow it as the subject.
longexplanation: The sentence opens with the modifying phrase "Having devised an optical spectroscopy technique...," which must be followed by the person who did the devising. Choice A places "chemist Ahmed Zewail" right after the comma, correctly identifying who devised the technique and introduced the discipline. Choices B and C make "a new scientific discipline" or "the introduction" the subject, illogically implying the discipline devised the technique. Choice D produces a fragment with no working main verb, so only A resolves the modifier correctly.

question:
London's Globe Theatre is a reconstruction of the celebrated venue where many of Shakespeare's plays were first performed. During a 1613 performance, a prop cannon ______ and ignited the Globe's thatched roof. Although no one was hurt, within two hours the original Globe was gone.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
tags: form structure and sense, verb tense
shortexplanation: The event happened in 1613, so the simple past "malfunctioned" is required.
longexplanation: The sentence describes a specific completed event in 1613 and pairs the blank with the past-tense verb "ignited," so the verb should also be in the simple past. "Malfunctioned" matches this past-tense context, making choice B correct. The present perfect "has malfunctioned" (A), present tense "malfunctions" (C), and future "will malfunction" (D) all clash with a clearly finished past event. Only the simple past keeps the sentence consistent.
